common_name: Celestial Star Gardenia (Cold-Hardy Compact Double White Gardenia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil; site in partial shade for best flowering and to avoid afternoon-sun leaf scorch in Gulf South gardens.

directions: Celestial Star produces large, double, swirled white flowers that open from spring into a heavy fall rebloom, carrying the classic intense gardenia fragrance on a compact, moderate-growing 4-foot shrub. It is a comparatively recent American selection noted for cold hardiness and heat tolerance. Grow in strongly acidic, evenly moist soil with afternoon shade in the Gulf South to prevent iron chlorosis and flower bleaching.

common_name: Star Bright Gardenia (Large Single Star-Shaped White Gardenia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; this older Florida-origin selection is a vigorous grower that benefits from Gulf South afternoon-shade siting.

directions: Star Bright was selected in the Gainesville, Florida area and is patented for its abundant large, single, star-shaped white flowers set against lush deep-green foliage. It is a vigorous grower well suited to Gulf South hedging and specimen use. Provide strongly acidic, humus-rich soil and afternoon shade to keep foliage dark green and flowers free of sun-bleaching.
sources: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (Plant Patent PP8,887)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; its compact, freely-branching habit suits foundation plantings and smaller Gulf South borders.

directions: Starlight was bred in Australia from an open-pollinated cross with 'Radicans' to produce a compact, densely branching gardenia with fragrant white flowers and glossy dark foliage. Its smaller stature fits containers and tight border spaces better than standard-size gardenias. Grow in strongly acidic, consistently moist soil with afternoon shade to avoid iron chlorosis in Gulf South landscapes.
sources: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (Plant Patent PP24,228)

common_name: Snow Globe Gardenia (Compact Rounded Single-Flowered Gardenia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; its tight, rounded 18-24 inch habit suits edging and small-space Gulf South plantings.

directions: Snow Globe, sold under the patented cultivar code 'WAH-SG', is a dense, tightly rounded dwarf gardenia growing only 18 to 24 inches tall and wide, with small, single, fragrant white flowers and glossy dark green foliage. Its diminutive scale makes it practical for containers, low borders, and foundation plantings where standard gardenias would be too large. Provide strongly acidic, evenly moist soil and afternoon shade in Gulf South gardens to prevent iron chlorosis.
sources: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (Plant Patent PP31,088)

common_name: Star Dust Gardenia (Nematode-Resistant Interspecific Hybrid Gardenia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; its nematode resistance is a particular advantage in sandy Gulf South soils where root-knot nematode pressure damages standard gardenias.

directions: Star Dust is a patented interspecific hybrid of Gardenia jasminoides and Gardenia thunbergia, bred for resistance to root-knot nematode (race 2) while retaining dark glossy foliage and fragrant white gardenia flowers. This nematode resistance makes it a useful choice on sandy Gulf Coast sites where nematodes limit standard gardenia performance. Grow in strongly acidic, humus-rich soil with afternoon shade for best results.
sources: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (Plant Patent PP21,541)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; its low, dense profile suits foundation plantings and small-space Gulf South gardens.

directions: Genie-2 was discovered as a seedling in Alachua County, Florida and selected for its dense, low-profile habit, dark green foliage, and abundant fragrant white flowers. Its heat tolerance and disease resistance suit the humid Gulf South, and its compact size fits small borders and foundation plantings. Grow in strongly acidic, consistently moist soil with afternoon shade to avoid iron chlorosis and flower bleaching.
sources: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (Plant Patent PP26,734)
